chunks: And from him, from Fadalah, from Saif, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you rise from the two rak'ahs, lean on your palms and say: 'By God's power I rise and I sit,' for Ali (peace be upon him) used to do that."
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and physical action when rising from the second rak'ah in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the prophetic tradition (sunnah) of leaning on the palms while rising from the second rak'ah, a practice specifically attributed to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) to demonstrate humility and reliance on divine strength. The recitation 'Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq'ud' (By God's power I rise and sit) serves as a concise dhikr, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on emulating the Ahl al-Bayt's precise ritual conduct (fiqh al-ibadat) as a means of spiritual connection.
